Engineers repaired a computer fifteen billion miles from Earth.
In November 2023, Voyager 1 started sending back gibberish.
The culprit was one dead memory chip inside its 1977 flight computer.
That chip held part of the software that packages Voyager's data.
And nobody can swap a chip in interstellar space.
So engineers split the code into pieces and hid them in free memory.
Every command took about twenty two and a half hours to arrive.
On April 20, 2024, readable data finally came home.
This month, Voyager 1 went quiet again, and engineers are still diagnosing it.
Can they fix a computer fifteen billion miles away twice?
